name: Cheesy Pork Chop and Hash Brown Casserole
intro_html: Seared pork chops on a bed of cheesy sour cream hash browns with buttery mushrooms and onions. This is diner comfort food built for the week ahead: 47 grams of protein and 672 calories per serving at about $3.90 (at everyday cost). Bring an appetite and a fork; the casserole handles the rest.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper): ~$0.20. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $46.86 across 14 servings, so roughly $3.35 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $54.19 across 14 servings, roughly $3.87 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.34 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $59.53. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.90 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a chop-and-potatoes plate a diner would ring up at four times that before you even order coffee.
shop_smart: Pork chops are the big line item, so watch for family packs on sale and stock the freezer; chops freeze and thaw with zero drama.
Frozen hash browns cost far less per pound than fresh potatoes once you count your shredding time, and there is no gray-potato panic.
White mushrooms in the 8 oz packs go on sale often. Compare per-ounce to the sliced ones; whole mushrooms are cheaper and slicing takes two minutes.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 350F. Season the pork chops with salt and pepper and sear them in a hot skillet, about 2 minutes per side, just for color. Set aside; they finish in the oven.
In the same skillet, melt the butter and cook the diced onions and sliced mushrooms 6 to 8 minutes until browned and their liquid has cooked off.
In your biggest bowl, mix the thawed hash browns, sour cream, chicken broth, the mushroom-onion mixture, half the cheddar, salt, and pepper.
Spread the hash brown mixture into two greased 9x13 pans and lay the seared chops on top.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes, then uncover, scatter the remaining cheddar over everything, and bake 10 to 15 more minutes until bubbly and the pork reaches at least 145F.
Rest 10 minutes, then cube the chops and fold everything together in your weighed pot so every portion gets pork, potatoes, and cheese.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each of 14 containers. Every bowl delivers 672 calories and 47 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Foodtastic Mom, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.

steps: Sear the seasoned pork chops 2 minutes per side and set aside.
Brown the onions and mushrooms in butter.
Mix hash browns, sour cream, broth, the mushroom mixture, and half the cheddar, then spread into two 9x13 pans.
Top with the chops, bake covered at 350F for 45 minutes, then uncovered with the rest of the cheese until the pork reaches 145F.
Rest, cube the chops, fold everything together, and portion into 14 containers.
